guides.wedding-gift-calculator.title: Wedding Gift Amount: What Is Actually Expected
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.desc: How guests choose a wedding gift amount, the role of the cost-per-head rule, regional customs and when cash or a registry item is right.
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.lead: There is no obligation to cover your plate. The amount depends on how close you are, your own budget, and what is customary where the wedding takes place.
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.f1v: Usually the most generous tier, often a substantial cash or registry gift
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.f2v: Commonly a mid-range gift, sometimes shared with a group
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.f3v: Often a modest group gift or a small registry item
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.f4v: Your relationship and budget matter more than the meal cost
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.s1: Start with what you can comfortably afford, then adjust for closeness, whether you are bringing a guest, and whether you have already paid for travel and accommodation. A group gift lets several people give something meaningful without each overspending. If there is a registry, using it is genuinely helpful to the couple.
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.s2: In the US registries are standard and cash gifts are common; some couples use a honeymoon fund. In the UK and much of Europe cash or a cheque is frequent, and a registry may be a small list or absent. In many Asian wedding cultures money is given in a ceremonial envelope at the event, with amounts sometimes chosen for auspicious numbers — follow the family's custom rather than a Western rule of thumb.
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.s3: Do not calculate a gift from an estimated per-head catering cost; that figure is private and varies by venue. Do not bring a large physical gift to the reception — the couple has to transport it. And send it reasonably close to the wedding or within a few months after, with a note so it can be acknowledged properly.
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.q1: Should a gift cover the cost of my meal?
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.a1: No. That is a guideline some guests use as a floor, not an obligation. Your relationship and your own budget are the right starting points.
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.a2: In most places yes, and in many cultures it is the norm. Use the couple's preferred method if they have indicated one.
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.q3: How late can I send a gift?
guides.wedding-gift-calculator.a3: Within a few months of the wedding is generally fine. Include a note with your full name so the thank-you card is addressed correctly.
